grades.quote: Implementations will not raise an exception on writes of unsupported values to a **WARL** field. Implementations can return any legal value on the read of a **WARL** field when the last write was of an illegal value, but the legal value returned should deterministically depend on the illegal written value and the architectural state of the hart.
grades.reason: Directly defines WARL: any value may be written, a legal value is always read back, no exception on unsupported writes, and the legal value read should depend deterministically on the written value and hart state. It does not cover WPRI or WLRL, so it answers only one of the three terms.
WPRI appears only as a field label in the stateen0 register figures. The passage never explains what WPRI, WLRL or WARL mean.

grades.quote: When HSXLEN=64, VSXL is a **WARL** field that is encoded the same as the MXL field of `misa` , shown in Table 9. In particular, an implementation may make VSXL be a read-only field whose value always ensures that VSXLEN=HSXLEN.
grades.reason: Gives a usage example of a WARL field (VSXL), including that it may be read-only. It does not define WARL, WPRI or WLRL, so it is only auxiliary.

grades.quote: When VSXLEN=64, UXL is a **WARL** field that is encoded the same as the MXL field of `misa` , shown in Table 9. In particular, an implementation may make UXL be a read-only copy of field VSXL of `hstatus` , forcing VU-mode XLEN=VSXLEN.
grades.reason: Gives a usage example of a WARL field (UXL) that may be read-only. It does not define the WPRI, WLRL or WARL semantics, so it is only auxiliary.
